title: The Strange Story of Sea Monkeys
summary: Hosts Josh Clark and Chuck Bryant explore the history of Sea Monkeys, the brine shrimp novelty pets marketed by Harold von Braunhut through comic book ads from the 1960s onward. They cover the product's creation (a hybrid of brine shrimp developed with help from a micro crustacean expert), the fantastical original booklet, the 1980s live-action TV show, and von Braunhut's other inventions and gimmicks (X-ray specs, Invisible Goldfish, Director Mat, the KiYoga Agent M5 telescoping whip). The bulk of the episode covers reports that von Braunhut was a white nationalist donor to the Aryan Nations and Richard Butler, a Jewish man born Harold Nathan Braunhut, a loan to a Klan grand wizard, and his death in 2003. The final part covers the ensuing legal fight between his widow Yolanda Signorelli von Braunhut and Big Time Toys over the Sea Monkeys brand, which involves knockoff products made in China. The episode closes with a listener mail about Pompeii lemons and a sign-off.

segments.title: Comic book memories and Sea Monkeys ads
segments.summary: Hosts swap childhood comic book memories, including Archie, Richie Rich, and 1960s comics read at a grandmother's house, then recall old ads for Sea Monkeys, X-ray specs, Charles Atlas, and Bonkers.

segments.title: Sea Monkey family illustration and the original ads
segments.summary: The hosts describe the royal Sea Monkey family illustrated by Joe Orlando and the fine print noting the figures are caricatures. They explain Sea Monkeys are not a natural species but a hybrid of brine shrimp created by a man-made breeding effort.

segments.title: Cryptobiosis and the secret formula
segments.summary: Sea Monkeys are brine shrimp eggs that enter cryptobiosis, a dried suspended state. The hosts explain the special powder that alters pH and salinity so they hatch quickly, and that the formula was known only to von Braunhut and his wife until his death in 2003.

segments.title: Von Braunhut's marketing and the booklet
segments.summary: Von Braunhut wrote a fantastical 32-page booklet describing trainable Sea Monkeys, and marketed directly to kids through comic book inserts after the failure of Whamo's Instant Fish. The hosts discuss the scale of his ad campaign and why kids ordering by mail mattered.

segments.title: Sea Monkeys TV show and von Braunhut's other inventions
segments.summary: The hosts describe the 1980s live-action Sea Monkeys TV show starring Howie Mandel. They then cover von Braunhut's other products, including X-ray specs, Invisible Goldfish, Battleship-style games, the doll eye patent, and the Director Mat.

segments.title: Von Braunhut's stunts and the KiYoga Agent M5
segments.summary: The hosts recount von Braunhut's background as a motorcycle and car racer, talent manager, and promoter of a high diver, then discuss the KiYoga Agent M5 telescoping whip, his arrest at LaGuardia, and its link to fundraising for Aryan Nations.

segments.title: White nationalist ties and Aryan Nations donations
segments.summary: The hosts explain documented ties between von Braunhut and white nationalist groups, especially the Aryan Nations and Richard Butler, including a newsletter linking the M5 sales to a defense fund. They discuss his Jewish birth, his Idaho rallies, the 1988 Washington Post exposé, and the reaction of licensing partners.

segments.title: Loan to KKK leader and death
segments.summary: The hosts describe von Braunhut loaning a Klan grand wizard twelve thousand dollars to buy firearms, his prepaid care for his Jewish parents' graves, and his death in 2003.

segments.title: Legal fight over the Sea Monkeys brand
segments.summary: The hosts cover the dispute between widow Yolanda von Braunhut and Big Time Toys, which claims ownership after licensing payments, and the knockoff Chinese products that reportedly fail to hatch. The hosts reflect on whether the brand will survive.

segments.title: Listener mail: Pompeii lemons and the lunch break joke
segments.summary: A listener corrects the hosts about cedri lemons near Pompeii, and another listener jokes about the hosts cutting out commercial break requests.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts give contact information for listener feedback and sign off.
